Subject: Discovery recap: inference unit-econ pressure + ops asks

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few concrete next steps so we all stay aligned. TL;DR: main pain is rising token costs on heavy LLM calls (high QPS with medium-length contexts), current infra is GPU burst on GCP, and the team is open to quantization if it preserves quality.

What we covered
- Current stack: quantrove inference service on GCP (n1 VMs + 1x A100 burst), custom batching but no KV prefix caching, requests mostly ~600 tokens average (1.2s p50 latency target).
- Pain points: token unit economics ballooning as feature usage scales (esp. reranking + chat flows), unpredictable tail latency during bursts, and limited telemetry for per-route cost attribution.
- Success criteria for a pilot: 40% reduction in per-inference token cost or equivalent ops savings, end-to-end p95 latency <= 2s for the two highest-volume routes, and transparent cost dashboarding per model/route.

Batching / caching / quantization notes from call
- Batching: they have a 50ms batching window today but only at the process level; scope to unify across services and move to continuous batching.
- Caching: they can adopt prefix/KV caching on stateless routes; the analytics team wants eviction visibility.
- Quantization: engineering is open to int8 if top-1 output fidelity is within 1-2% of FP16 on our eval set.

Immediate asks / next steps (owner in parentheses)
1) I will send a short pilot outline + a sample cost model for them to review (attached) — Lukas (today).
2) Quantrove to share a small set of representative prompts / eval examples and one week's request trace (anonymized) so we can estimate batching/caching gains — Samir/Priya (EOD Mon 9/21).
3) Ben + Marissa: run a quick feasibility pass on quantization risk for the model family they mentioned (LLM-xlarge) and map potential perf wins — Ben/Marissa (EOW Wed 9/23).
4) Schedule 30m ops deep-dive to map telemetry and networking constraints (Samir, Lukas) — propose times below.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-outline.pdf (pilot scope + SLOs), sample-cost-model.csv (example unit-econ calc)

If that aligns, I’ll queue a 30m follow-up and Ben will prepare an initial quantization signal report.

Thanks —

Thanks Lukas — this looks right and helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 600-token average was across user-facing chat + a nightly batch rerank job. The rerank job is the heaviest token sink.
- We can extract a 48-hour anonymized trace by Monday morning.
- For evals, we'll send ~200 gold prompts (rank+chat) and a small labeled set for the reranker.

Two small asks: can you include estimated latency impact of prefix caching (ballpark)? Also want to confirm that Redwood supports mixed-routing (hosted for low-volume, dedicated for heavy rerank jobs) — that architecture is important to our infra team.

Happy to take the 30m ops slot next Tue 9/22 9:30–10:00 PT or Wed 9/23 8:00–8:30 PT.

Samir

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference unit-econ pressure + ops asks

Appreciate the quick reply, Samir — all good. Short answers:
- Prefix caching: based on similar workloads we’ve seen, prefix/KV caching can reduce token-generation spend by 20–50% for routes with high prefix overlap; latency impact is usually neutral-to-positive on p95 because cache hits avoid full attention passes but depends on cache hit ratio and eviction policy. We’ll include a conservative sim in the pilot doc.
- Mixed-routing: yes — Redwood supports mixed topologies (hosted API for interactive, Dedicated pools for high-throughput rerank). We’ll map model variants and fallback policies in the pilot scope.

I’ll confirm the ops slot for Tue 9/22 9:30 PT and send calendar invite. Ben / Marissa — can you confirm availability?

Lukas

Looping in my quick quantization notes (more formal readout on Wed). Key bullets:
- For LLM-xlarge family, we get decent int8 throughput gains on A100 and H100 with minimal quality regression in our internal evals; some attention heads are sensitive, so we recommend a hybrid approach (fp16 for sensitive layers).
- Expected perf: 1.8–2.5x token throughput increase depending on kernel path and sequence length; memory reductions can enable larger batching windows.
- Risks: retraining not required but we should run small calibration and a 1000-example fidelity sweep.

I’ve accepted the 9:30 PT slot and will bring a short checklist for data/trace formatting.
